You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

What do you mean by “rich visitor”? Here are a few common SQL interpretations—pick one and I’ll tailor it:

### Option A: Visitors who spent the most (total across all visits)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
```

### Option B: Visitors who spent above a threshold (e.g., > 1000)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
HAVING SUM(vi.Total_spent) > 1000
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
```

### Option C: Visitors with the highest single-visit spend
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  MAX(vi.Total_spent) AS max_single_visit_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY max_single_visit_spent DESC;
```

Tell me which definition you want (A/B/C), and if you want **top N** (e.g., top 5) or a **minimum spend** cutoff.
focus on the visitor who bought the most tickets

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_tickets DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

If you want to include ties (multiple visitors with the same max tickets), tell me your SQL dialect (SQLite/MySQL/Postgres) and I’ll adjust.
Also should get the visitor's name in the details.

This returns the visitor who bought the most tickets **and includes the visitor name**:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_tickets DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
also need to make sure the ticket purchase was done in a single transaction

To ensure the “most tickets” were bought **in a single transaction (one row in `visit`)**, rank by `Num_of_Ticket` per visit row:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.Num_of_Ticket,
  vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY vi.Num_of_Ticket DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

If you want to return *all* ties (multiple transactions with the same max `Num_of_Ticket`), tell me your SQL dialect (SQLite/MySQL/Postgres).
also need to get the visitor's age along with the name

```sql
SELECT
  v.Name,
  v.Age,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.Num_of_Ticket
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY vi.Num_of_Ticket DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
